fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. Moses, Israel's leader, and Aaron go to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, with a message. They say the LORD, the God of Israel, says, “Let My people go, so that they may hold a feast to Me in the wilderness.” (Exodus 5:1) A feast is a gathering, and this one is for the LORD. I love a good gathering, so this message has my vote.

I see why you'd think so, but this message doesn't mention a permanent move. Moses and Aaron tell Pharaoh the LORD, the God of Israel, says, “Let My people go, so that they may hold a feast to Me in the wilderness.” (Exodus 5:1) The request is for a feast to the LORD. Going back for good isn't part of it.

Hungry makes sense for people working that hard, but Pharaoh doesn't go there. He tells the taskmasters, “For they are lazy; that is why they are crying out, ‘Let us go and sacrifice to our God.’” (Exodus 5:8) He gives them a label, not a need. I think that says a lot about how he sees them.

The wilderness is where Moses and Aaron asked to go for the feast, but that's not what this verse says. “So the people scattered all over the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.” (Exodus 5:12) The text puts the search all over Egypt. I bet that was one exhausting scavenger hunt.

Nothing in the verse says secret. The LORD says, “because of My strong hand he will drive them out of his land.” (Exodus 6:1) Drive is the word He uses, and the verse doesn't say anything about sneaking. A secret exit sounds more like me slipping a cookie off the cooling rack.
